What AI consulting for small business looks like here

AI consulting for small business should end with a short, ranked list you can act on, not a slide deck about the future of work.

Most owners who call us have heard that AI can answer phones, write emails and run marketing, and they want to know which of that applies to a business their size. The SBA's own guidance on AI for small business makes the same point we do: AI is relatively new, so start small, and when you use free AI tools, have another person review what they produce. Its Office of Advocacy reported in September 2025, using Census Bureau survey data, that AI use among small firms (fewer than 250 employees) rose from 6.3 percent to 8.8 percent over six months. In other words, most small businesses are not using it yet, and there is no penalty for deciding carefully.

As an AI consultant for small business, our job is to find the one or two changes that would actually make a difference this quarter, explain what they would cost, and say plainly where AI would be the wrong tool.

The questions we ask first

The first conversation is mostly questions. These are the ones that shape the recommendation:

  • How do customers reach you today: phone, website, walk-ins, referrals, ads?
  • When do calls come in that nobody answers, and what happens to them?
  • What do callers ask most often, and could someone new answer it from a sheet?
  • Which tasks do you or your staff repeat every day or every week?
  • Where do leads or appointments fall through the cracks?
  • What software do you already use for booking, billing or jobs?
  • What information do customers share with you that must stay private?
  • Which questions must never be answered by anyone but you or a licensed person?
  • What would a mistake cost: an apology, a refund, a lost client, a compliance problem?

How we decide what to automate first: a scoring checklist

Each candidate task gets a score from 0 to 2 on six questions. Higher totals go first. A 0 on the last two questions can take a task off the list no matter how high it scores elsewhere.

Question012
How often does it happen?Monthly or lessWeeklyDaily
Does it follow the same steps each time?RarelyMostlyAlmost always
Is it lost when nobody is available?NoSometimesOften: after hours, weekends, busy days
Can the answer come from facts you approve?No, it needs judgmentPartlyYes
Is a mistake cheap to catch and fix?No: legal, medical, financial or safety stakesUsuallyYes
Can it be done without sensitive data?NoWith careYes

Answering routine calls after hours tends to score high for a local service business. Quoting a price for unseen work, giving legal or medical answers, and handling patient records score low, and we tell you so.

What you get out of it

An order of work

A ranked list: what to automate first, what second, and what to leave with people. Usually it starts with how calls and inquiries are answered.

A fit check

Which of our published services, if any, would cover the top items, and at what price. If something we do not offer would serve you better, we say so.

The limits in writing

What the AI would not be allowed to say or decide for your business, so the rules are settled before anything is built.

If you then want us to build it, the same notes become the setup: the facts your AI voice agent answers from, the workflows in your CRM, and the questions it hands to you.

Risks to weigh before you add AI

A good AI consultant spends as much time on risk as on features. These are the ones that come up for almost every small business.

Privacy and data

Callers and chat visitors tell an AI system things: names, addresses, sometimes health or legal details. Decide what it should collect, what it should never ask for, and who can see the records. A May 2026 GAO report on AI in SBA programs named data privacy and security among the main risks of AI use. Nothing we set up is a HIPAA compliance program.

Accuracy

AI can sound confident and still be wrong. The same GAO report listed inaccurate outputs and automation bias, the tendency to over-trust automated outputs, as risks, and its expert panel said including human review can reduce some of them. That is why our agents answer from facts you approve, hand off what they do not know, and get reviewed after real calls.

What you claim about it

If you advertise that your business uses AI, the claim has to be true. The FTC has warned businesses to keep their AI claims in check, and its 2024 enforcement sweep, Operation AI Comply, made clear there is no AI exemption from the laws against deceptive advertising.

A way to think it through

NIST's AI Risk Management Framework is voluntary guidance built around four functions: govern, map, measure and manage. A small business does not need the full framework, but the habit fits: decide who is responsible, know where AI is used, check how it performs, and fix what goes wrong.

Why the consultant also builds

Plenty of AI consultant services stop at a recommendation and leave you to find someone to carry it out. We are an AI agency that does the setup, so the advice is tied to things we actually configure on HighLevel and maintain afterward: AI receptionists and voice agents, website chat, booking, CRM automation and business automation.

That has a downside worth naming: an agency that sells setup has a reason to recommend setup. Our answer is to show prices up front, tell you when the first step is something you can do yourself for free, and let you call our AI receptionist before you decide whether you want one at all.

We do not build custom AI models or software products, and we do not give legal, medical or tax advice. If your question is in that territory, we will tell you to ask someone licensed.

What AI consulting does not include

What you can expect

  • Questions about your business before any recommendation
  • A ranked list of what to automate first, and what not to
  • Plain prices for anything we would set up
  • An honest note when AI is not the right fix

What it does not do

  • Give legal, medical, tax or financial advice
  • Act as a HIPAA compliance program or review clinical or patient-record handling
  • Build custom AI models or software products
  • Promise results, savings or a return on investment
  • Confirm a connection to your current software before we have tested it for your account

Questions owners ask about AI consulting

What does an AI consultant do?

An AI consultant helps a business decide where AI is worth using, which tools fit, and what could go wrong. For a small business that is mostly practical: looking at how customers reach you, which tasks repeat, and where a mistake would hurt, then recommending a short list of changes in order. Some consultants stop at advice. We also set up what we recommend, but only if you want us to.

How can AI help small businesses?

The clearest uses are the ones with a lot of repetition and a low cost of error: answering the phone when nobody can, answering the same website questions, booking appointments, logging inquiries and sending routine follow-up. AI can also help with drafting marketing copy and summarizing calls. It is weaker at anything that needs judgment, a license or a look at the actual job, and those parts should stay with you.

How much do AI consultants charge?

Independent consultants set their own rates, and we do not publish a separate consulting price. Here the AI consulting is part of the setup conversation: we talk through your business, recommend what to automate first, and tell you which of our published services would fit, if any. Our services and packages, with prices, are on the pricing page.

Is there an AI consultant near me?

Dominion AI Agency is run from East Texas and takes on small businesses anywhere in the 50 states, entirely remotely. Consulting happens by phone, email and shared screens, and nothing we set up needs a visit. If you want to hear what an AI phone agent sounds like before you talk to anyone, call our main line: the AI receptionist that answers is one we configured.

What can AI do for my business?

That depends on where your business loses time or customers today, which is why we ask before we answer. For many local businesses it starts with the phone: an AI receptionist that answers when you cannot, takes a message and books. For others it is the website, the follow-up, or reviews. For a few, the honest answer is that a simpler fix, such as a better voicemail or clearer hours online, comes first.

Hear the AI receptionist answer before you buy one
